result.title: Evolve to Learn: Gradient-aligned experience evolution for model self-improvement
result.summary: Self-evolving language models can continuously acquire useful experience through test-time interaction, reflection, and prompt optimization, yet turning such experience into model itself to ensure self improvement remains challenging. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides a natural mechanism for internalizing test-time information into model parameters, yet it largely assumes that the gener- ated experience is worth learning. We show that this assumption does not always hold: experiences that improve test-time performance may provide limited or even harmful training signals. To better characterize which experience should be inter- nalized, we systematically analyze diverse mutated experiences across multiple tasks and reflection models, and find that gradient-based alignment is a more reli- able indicator of downstream distillation gains than immediate test-time improve- ment. Based on this finding, we propose E2L, a self-evolution framework that iteratively generates, evaluates, and distills experiences according to their esti- mated training utility. E2L closes the loop between experience generation and parameter learning, enabling agents to autonomously produce experience suitable for self-improvement.

AI.brief_summary: 该文指出现有 on-policy 自蒸馏默认「测试时有效的经验就值得学习」，通过多任务、多反思模型的系统性分析发现梯度对齐度比即时测试表现更能预测蒸馏收益，并提出 E2L 框架按估计的训练效用来生成、筛选并蒸馏经验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以梯度对齐而非表面表现筛选待内化轨迹」的思路，可能为 LVR 中哪些 latent 推理轨迹值得训练、如何做贡献分配与监督筛选提供可核查的方法线索；但纯文本设定，与视觉证据保留无直接关系。
